blocks.t: F i g u r e 14.14 (a) In a column chromatograph, the top of the column is loaded with a mixture of solutes to be separated (green). (b) Upon addition of solvent, the different solutes travel at different rates, giving rise to bands. The separate fractions can be collected in different flasks for use or analysis.

F i g u r e 14.15 In a gas–liquid chromatograph, the sample is vaporized and passes through a column, carried in a stream of an inert gas such as helium or nitrogen. The residence time of any substance on the column depends on its partition coefficient from the vapor to the liquid in the column. A species leaving the column at a given time can be detected by a variety of techniques. The result is a gas chromatogram, with a peak corresponding to each substance in the mixture.
